summary: Runner code was already in place; under the new rule (a time is measured and recorded, not a gate) I measured it and wrote it down. TEST_JOBS=4: 207 s wall, 392/392, slowest file 156 s, floor 203 s (811 s of slot time / 4), peak 254 MB. TEST_JOBS=1: 758 s. Same per-file counts and PASS names at 1 and 4 jobs. Decision file, CLAUDE.md, README and architecture updated.
verified_how: TEST_JOBS=4 bash tests/run.sh in a 3G user scope: rc 0, 392/392, wall 207 s, memory.peak 266801152 B; TEST_JOBS=1: 392/392, 758 s, per-file counts and C-sorted PASS names cmp-equal; bash -n on run.sh, lib.sh and every tests/checks/*.sh; lib/check.sh green in 205 s (392/392)

discoveries.text: The suite is now work-bound, not chain-bound: the 4-job floor (811 s / 4 = 203 s) is above the slowest file (156 s), so reordering files gains nothing. Only cutting CPU (fewer node starts in the driver) would make it shorter. Four jobs' contention adds about 56 s of slot time over TEST_JOBS=1's 755 s.
